word_translation_en: to lead into; to flow into; to result in
word_translation_ru: впадать (о реке); приводить к чему-либо; заканчиваться чем-либо
sentence_example: Der kleine Fluss mündet schließlich in die Elbe.
sentence_example_translation_en: The small river finally flows into the Elbe.
sentence_example_translation_ru: Маленькая река в конце концов впадает в Эльбу.
sentence_synonym: Der kleine Fluss fließt schließlich in die Elbe.
typical_collocations: in den Ozean münden; in einer Sackgasse münden; in einen Streit münden; direkt münden
usage_comments_en: Governs the preposition 'in' followed by the accusative case (especially for physical water flow/direction) or dative case (often used for metaphorical outcomes, e.g., 'in einem Fiasko münden'). It is used literally for bodies of water and roads, and figuratively for situations that lead to a specific result.

word_translation_en: to discharge; to empty; to open into
sentence_example: Der Abwasserkanal mündet direkt im Meer aus.
sentence_example_translation_en: The sewer canal discharges directly into the sea.
sentence_example_translation_ru: Канализационный канал выходит прямо в море.
sentence_synonym: Der Abwasserkanal mündet direkt ins Meer.
typical_collocations: im Meer ausmünden; in ein Becken ausmünden; im Freien ausmünden
usage_comments_en: A formal and relatively rare separable verb. It is primarily used in technical contexts (such as architecture, plumbing, or engineering) or anatomy to describe where a pipe, canal, or vessel empties. It is often constructed with 'in' + dative.

word_translation_en: to flow into; to merge; to join (a road)
sentence_example: Die Nebenstraße mündet in die Hauptstraße ein.
sentence_example_translation_en: The side street merges into the main road.
sentence_example_translation_ru: Второстепенная дорога примыкает к главной улице.
sentence_synonym: Die Nebenstraße führt direkt auf die Hauptstraße.
typical_collocations: in die Autobahn einmünden; in einen Fluss einmünden; rechtwinklig einmünden
usage_comments_en: A separable verb. It is highly similar to 'münden' but is preferred when describing roads, traffic lanes, or tributaries joining a larger network. It governs the preposition 'in' + accusative.

word_translation_en: mouth (of a river); muzzle (of a gun); orifice
sentence_example: Wir bauten unser Zelt nahe der Mündung des Flusses auf.
sentence_example_translation_en: We set up our tent near the mouth of the river.
sentence_example_translation_ru: Мы разбили палатку у устья реки.
sentence_synonym: Wir bauten unser Zelt nahe dem Ende des Flusses auf.
typical_collocations: die Mündung des Rheins; an der Mündung; Gewehrmündung; direkt vor der Mündung
usage_comments_en: A feminine noun (die Mündung). It is primarily used to describe the geographical mouth of a river. In military or hunting contexts, it refers to the muzzle (the open end of a gun barrel).
